evidence:
REJECT for materiality, not because the version barrier is absent. At frozen 3abee5a6, src/store/connection.rs:167-175 opens the actual store and calls initialize; src/store/schema.rs:689-705 applies V36, sets user_version=36 and commits that step separately, then :708-826 advances through V45. The named published base 565def86 has LATEST_VERSION=35 (schema.rs:74), accepts 18..=35 and rejects higher versions with IncompatibleSchema (:427-432). The append-only migration diff adds 0036..0045 and leaves 0001..0035 unchanged. No reverse-migration or database-preimage path exists in the reviewed initializer/open_writer chain. Thus executable-only rollback cannot reopen the upgraded durable instance, including when V36 succeeds and V37 later fails. Fetched primary grounding: [SQLite user_version](https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html#pragma_user_version) says it stores the integer 'at offset 60 in the database header'; [SQLite transactions](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_transaction.html) says transactions 'usually persist until the next COMMIT or ROLLBACK command'. These are application schema decisions, not SQLite file-format incompatibility.

However, the finding does not demonstrate violation of this change's supported contract. I searched all eleven named design documents and TRUST/README/install/operations/release guidance for rollback, downgrade, reverse/down migration, backup/snapshot, restore and equivalent compatibility wording. The specified upgrade/rollback/reopen requirements concern forward migration, preserved historical rows/digests/FKs, rollback of the failing transactional step, and reopening/retrying with the candidate; there is no executable-only downgrade guarantee or schema backup requirement. The parent design explicitly requires upgrading dormant obligations (:24), authorizes additive schema work, and excludes deployment (:63,80). The composition proof makes rollback adjacent to foreign_keys restoration and catalog preservation (upstream-478ec4a9-composition-plan.md:33-35). Actual tests demonstrate the intended meaning: tests/store/schema.rs:7956-8028 injects failed V45 DDL, retains V44, then repairs/retries/reopens; :8190-8278 injects failed V37, explicitly expects version36, preserves published ACK/binding/history, then retries/reopens with the candidate. These tests are source evidence, not a claim I ran them.

The surrounding repository expressly documents unknown-schema refusal without rewriting history (docs/operations.md:153). The base already advances prior versions in independently committed one-way steps (565def86 schema.rs:653-669,674-689); the new v36 boundary follows that existing architecture. The claimed 'new hook downgrade warning' also overstates its ancestry: the diff changes the existing warning at base src/harness/setup.rs:2942 from '--event' to 'hook-event', retaining the same unsetup-first advice (candidate :3282-3284). It addresses hook registration syntax and never promises that unsetup reverses a database upgrade. The specific v36 barrier is new, so I am not labeling this exact endpoint preExisting; rather, an executable-only rollback requirement would be a new operational guarantee. No data-loss mechanism or failure of the stated forward-upgrade/preservation contract is established by this finding.
